title: HighDimensionalHessianLipschitzPL.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: The class permits nonconvex objectives. The Hessian may be indefinite away from a minimizer while the global PL inequality holds.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HessianLipschitzPL.lean, spec.admissible, as used by LongTails/Setups/HighDimensionalHessianLipschitzPL.lean, spec.admissible.

problem_class.label: pl
problem_class.details: The objective attains its minimum f⋆ and satisfies the global Polyak–Łojasiewicz inequality 2μ(f(x) − f⋆) ≤ ‖∇f(x)‖² for every x ∈ ℝᵈ.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: The second component is the full Euclidean gradient at the query point.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: A single query at any x ∈ ℝᵈ returns the exact triple (f(x), ∇f(x), ∇²f(x)) for every history and oracle seed.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: The third component is the full Hessian as a linear operator on ℝᵈ, available in the same call.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HighDimensionalHessianLipschitzPL.lean, spec.Reply. LongTails/Setups/HessianLipschitzPL.lean, spec.admissible, fderiv ℝ (gradient f) x.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The domain is Euclidean ℝᵈ with x₀ = 0. The public dimension satisfies 2¹⁶⁰ ≤ H²Δ/μ³ ≤ d.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The gradient is differentiable and ‖∇²f(x) − ∇²f(y)‖op ≤ H‖x − y‖ globally. The initial gap satisfies f(0) − f⋆ ≤ Δ. All five parameters d, H, μ, Δ, ε are public, with H, μ, ε > 0 and 32ε ≤ Δ.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HighDimensionalHessianLipschitzPL.lean, Params, toGeneral, spec.publicInput and spec.valid. LongTails/Setups/HessianLipschitzPL.lean, spec.admissible.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The returned point X ∈ ℝᵈ is assessed by its objective gap f(X) − f⋆. It may be any point output from the algorithm’s state.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HighDimensionalHessianLipschitzPL.lean, spec.Output and spec.successful. LongTails/Setups/HessianLipschitzPL.lean, spec.successful. LongTails/Template.lean, Algorithm.output.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The output must be measurable, its objective gap integrable, and 𝔼[f(X) − f⋆] ≤ ε. The algorithm may randomize under the fixed oracle-call budget.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HessianLipschitzPL.lean, spec.successful. LongTails/Template.lean, Algorithm.law, executeWithTrace and Convergence.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The setup couples global PL geometry and a Lipschitz Hessian with full second-order access in the specific high-dimensional regime 2¹⁶⁰ ≤ H²Δ/μ³ ≤ d.

descriptionHtml:
High-Dimensional Hessian-Lipschitz PL Minimization

We consider minimizing a possibly nonconvex function f:Rd→R in dimension d. Its Hessian is H-Lipschitz, and it satisfies the Polyak–Łojasiewicz inequality with constant μ>0. The objective gap from the origin to a global minimizer x⋆ is at most Δ, with H>0 and 2160≤H2Δ/μ3≤d. At each query point, the oracle returns the exact value, gradient, and Hessian of f. For a tolerance 0<ε≤Δ/32, the goal is a measurable output x¯∈Rd with integrable gap satisfying E[f(x¯)−f(x⋆)]≤ε, where the expectation is over the algorithm’s randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Rdf(x). The algorithm receives d∈N and the real parameters H,μ,Δ,ε. The starting point is fixed at x0=0. We use the Euclidean norm ∥⋅∥ and its induced operator norm ∥⋅∥op.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Lipschitz Hessian). The function f and its gradient are Fréchet differentiable everywhere. At each x∈Rd, the Hessian ∇2f(x) is a linear operator on Rd, and for every x,y∈Rd, ∥∇2f(x)−∇2f(y)∥op≤H∥x−y∥.

Assumption 2 (Initial gap and gradient dominance). There exists a global minimizer x⋆∈Rd such that f(x0)−f(x⋆)≤Δ,2μ(f(x)−f(x⋆))≤∥∇f(x)∥2for every x∈Rd.

A query at any x∈Rd returns (f(x),∇f(x),∇2f(x)). After the allotted oracle calls, the output x¯ must be measurable, the gap f(x¯)−f(x⋆) must be integrable, and its expectation must satisfy E[f(x¯)−f(x⋆)]≤ε.

theorems.formulaHtml: ⌊(H2⋅Δμ3)14239⌋+

comparisonHtml:
On Rd, f has an H-Lipschitz Hessian in operator norm, an attained minimum f⋆, initial gap f(0)−f⋆≤Δ, and satisfies 2μ(f(x)−f⋆)≤∥∇f(x)∥2 globally. All parameters are public. Each joint query returns exact (f,∇f,∇2f) at one point. The target is a measurable output X with integrable gap and ∫(f(X)−f⋆)dP≤ε under the algorithm’s seed law P. Here H,μ,ε>0, 32ε≤Δ, and 2160≤A≤d.

Necessary oracle budgets for high-dimensional Hessian-Lipschitz PL minimization.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) HessianLipschitzPLLowerBound (Ours) (⋆⋆⋆) (review) Lower bound Ω((H2Δ/μ3)1/4) joint calls, randomized
(2) (Kornowski and Shamir 2021), Thm. 1 (k=2), strongly convex subclass Lower bound Ω((HD/μ)2/7+log⁡(1+log+⁡(μ3/(H2ε)))) joint calls, deterministic (1): Covers nonconvex PL objectives and randomized algorithms. At D≤2Δ/μ, the polynomial term in (2) is at most order A1/7 versus A1/4 in (1). Distance control alone does not certify the gap cap. (1): No doubly logarithmic accuracy term in the regime of (2), which requires D>Cmax{μ/H,(μ/H)5/12} and ε<cμ3/H2.
(3) (Yue et al. 2023), Thm. 3, L-smooth PL Lower bound Ω((L/μ)log⁡(Δ/ε)) gradient calls, deterministic (1): Second-order hardness for randomized algorithms without a gradient-Lipschitz bound. Rates are incomparable: the hard instance in (3) is not twice differentiable. (1): No accuracy logarithm. (3) applies for sufficiently large L/μ and ε≤Δ/16.
(4) (Carmon et al. 2020), Thm. 2 (p=2), smooth nonconvex stationarity Lower bound Ω(ΔHεg−3/2) all-derivative calls, randomized (1): Globally PL hard instances for objective-gap accuracy. At εg2≍μΔ the formulas have the same order. The rates are incomparable because the hard instances in (4) fail PL and the targets differ. (1): Larger required dimension at that scaling, d≥A versus order A1/2log⁡A in (4).

Abbr: A=H2Δ/μ3; D bounds initial distance to a minimizer; L is the gradient Lipschitz constant; εg targets ∥∇f∥≤εg; log+⁡t=max{0,log⁡t}; c,C are positive universal constants.

Carmon, Yair, John C. Duchi, Oliver Hinder, and Aaron Sidford. 2020. “Lower Bounds for Finding Stationary Points I.” Mathematical Programming 184: 71–120. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10107-019-01406-y.

import LongTails.Setups.HessianLipschitzPL
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Lp.MeasurableSpace
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.Real

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.HighDimensionalHessianLipschitzPL

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  d : ℕ
  H : ℝ
  μ : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

noncomputable def toGeneral (q : Params) : LongTails.Setups.HessianLipschitzPL.Params where
  E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d)
  H := q.H
  x0 := 0
  μ := q.μ
  Δ := q.Δ
  ε := q.ε

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance q := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d) → ℝ
  Query q := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d)
  Reply q := ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d) ×
    (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d) →L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d))
  Output q := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d)
  publicInput q := q
  valid q := 0 < q.H ∧ 0 < q.μ ∧ 0 < q.ε ∧ 32 * q.ε ≤ q.Δ ∧
    2 ^ 160 ≤ q.H ^ 2 * q.Δ / q.μ ^ 3 ∧ q.H ^ 2 * q.Δ / q.μ ^ 3 ≤ q.d
  admissible q f O := LongTails.Setups.HessianLipschitzPL.spec.admissible (toGeneral q) f O
  successful q f output P :=
    LongTails.Setups.HessianLipschitzPL.spec.successful (toGeneral q) f output P

end LongTails.Setups.HighDimensionalHessianLipschitzPL
